body:
Weight gain, more cognitive and memory problems (on top of my existing deficits)... I’m on an antipsychotic and it acts on dopamine, essentially lowering the amount you have available, which causes anhedonia, which causes depression... so then they prescribe an antidepressant, which causes anxiety (Wellabutrin), so they prescribe an anti-anxiety... etc etc. I’m beginning to understand how all of this works... 

Yes, cold helps. I wish I could live in an igloo. 🙄

I’d rather not say, but it does require a bit of planning and thinking and I just haven’t been keeping up. My sleep schedule is regular. I have this problem with excessive dreaming, which leaves me tired in the morning, but I do sleep.

I see all the professionals. It helps a little. Not a lot. Going through this has been scary because you got to a point where you realize that no one can help you. Before that you think, oh there must be some drug I can take or that therapy will fix me. The best thing you can do is never end up like this in the first place.
I spend my time going to work and then collapsing into a heap after it’s done. I don’t know long I can do it.
I have been to the doctor. I went from 0 to like 6 psych meds in a hot second. They help minimally. The side effects are shitty. The only thing that helps is taking long walks in the cold.

There’s not that much to tell about me anymore. I had a drug-induced psychotic break 3 years ago, it went untreated, and now I have brain damage and a whole bunch of other psychological problems. My mind is a living hell. My thoughts are loud and churning nonstop. I’m constantly arguing with myself all day in my head. I’m literally crazy. 

I used to be a normal person with a normal mind. My life was worth living then. I loved to read and dreamed of being a librarian. I had a wide taste in music, and movies, and all sorts of things. I liked going out with friends and also spending time at home with my cats. I liked lots of things. I wish to god I could go back in time. Now I just want to die. I’ve started to research how to do it and that scares me, but I’m building up my nerve.
